draft.title: Persuasion in spoken texts
card: In a speech, podcast or video, a speaker persuades with the voice as well as the words. The same sentence can sound different, and so have a different effect, depending on how it is said.
Intonation is the rise and fall of the voice. Stress is extra force on one word. A speaker can stress a word to make the audience notice it, as in "This is *our* town".
Volume is how loud the voice is. Pace is how fast the speaker talks. A louder voice can show anger or urgency. A slow pace can make a point sound serious and give listeners time to take it in.
A pause is a short silence. A pause before an important point builds attention. A pause after it gives listeners time to think about it.
draft.remember: Voice choices such as stress, volume, pace and pauses shape how an audience reacts to the words.

a.q: A speaker says, "We have one chance to fix this," then stays silent for three seconds before continuing. What is the likely effect of the silence?
opts: It gives the audience time to think about the point
It shows the speaker has forgotten what to say
It makes the point sound less important
It speeds up the speech and adds urgency
a.why: A pause after a main point lets it sink in, so the audience thinks about it. The silence does not make the point weaker. It is a planned choice, not a sign the speaker has lost their place.
a.clue: What do listeners do during a silence after a big claim?

b.q: In a school assembly, Jada speaks slowly and quietly about a classmate who was left out, then raises her volume and stresses the word "never" in "This must never happen again." What does the change in volume and stress mainly do?
opts: Signals strong feeling and draws attention to the demand
Shows that she is nervous and unsure of her view
Slows the speech so listeners can take in each word
Changes the topic so the audience hears a new idea
b.why: Raising volume and stressing "never" makes the demand stand out and shows strong feeling. The slow, quiet start is what gives time to take in the words, which is a different effect from the rise in volume. The change does not introduce a new topic.
b.clue: Think about which word is stressed, and what a louder voice usually shows.

a.best: It gives the audience time to think about the point

b.best: Signals strong feeling and draws attention to the demand
